_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES USED: idx 2, 4, 6 ONLY. Full page map, all 8 indices accounted for and each opened at full size, not just on the contact sheet: idx0 = cover (bilingual, 'Page 1 of 8', SET-3, Q.P. Code 65/1/3); idx1 = HINDI General Instructions + Q1-6; idx2 = ENGLISH General Instructions + SECTION A Q1-6 ('Page 3 of 8'); idx3 = HINDI khand-kha Q7-10 + khand-ga header + Q11; idx4 = ENGLISH SECTION B Q7-10 + SECTION C header + Q11 ('Page 5 of 8'); idx5 = HINDI Q12-14; idx6 = ENGLISH Q12-14 ('Page 7 of 8'); idx7 = 'Page 8 of 8', BLANK apart from a QR code, an asterisk and the footer. The booklet is chunked Hindi-then-English per BLOCK, not page-alternating end-to-end, so there are only three English pages. NO OVERFLOW of one language onto the other's page: idx3 opens at the top with the Hindi Section-B header and idx5 opens at the top with Hindi Q12, i.e. each Hindi block STARTS a page, so no English sat at the top of any odd index - checked on the full-size pages, not assumed. Continuity corroborates it: the three English pages carry Q1-6, Q7-11 and Q12-14 with every question complete and its printed marks visible, so no English content is missing. STRUCTURE (printed General Instructions, idx2): three Sections; A = Q1-6 short answer type-I @2, B = Q7-10 short answer type-II @3, C = Q11-14 long answer @4, and (vii) Question No. 14 is a case based problem with 2 subparts of 2 marks each. Marks 12+12+16 = 40, matching the cover's Maximum Marks : 40, Time allowed : 2 hours, 14 questions. NO MCQs anywhere - every row is subjective, so no options, no answer letters, and no key re-derivation applies. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads only 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO count, so the count was established by reading every question on the English pages and then confirmed question-by-question against the official 65/1/3 marking scheme, which reprints both branches under an 'OR'. FOUR internal choices: Q4, Q7, Q10, Q13. Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q9, Q11, Q12, Q14 carry no alternative. 19 rows = 14 questions + 4 OR-alternatives + 1 extra case-study sub-part. OVERLAP WITH 65/1/1: 14 of the 19 rows are the SAME QUESTIONS RESHUFFLED AND RENUMBERED, judged by reading each question on this paper's own page and comparing its content against data/2022-65-1-1.questions.json - not by plan.txt, which reported 0 already-covered and 13 to transcribe, i.e. it missed the overlap entirely (its two perceptual hints, Q3~65-1-1 Q2 and Q6~65-1-1 Q8, are BOTH wrong: this Q3 is 65/1/1's Q1 and this Q6 is new to the set). The mapping is this Q1=65/1/1 Q4, Q2=Q5, Q3=Q1, Q4a/b=Q3a/b, Q5=Q6, Q7a/b=Q9a/b, Q10a/b=Q7a/b, Q11=Q12, Q12=Q13, Q14i/ii=Q14i/ii; their stems and context are reused BYTE-FOR-BYTE from the reference file so they dedup at commit. GENUINELY NEW to this set: Q6 (dot product, perpendicular sum and difference), Q8 (line meets plane through three points), Q9 (homogeneous ODE) and BOTH branches of Q13 (area by integration) - 5 rows. SYLLABUS NOTE: this is the COVID-era Term-2 paper set on the PRE-rationalisation syllabus, and Q5 and Q8 both examine the PLANE in 3-D, filed on the 'The Plane' subtopic added 2026-08-19 for exactly this corpus. PRINTING NOTE: Q13's two branches are printed with NO (a)/(b) labels - only a bare 'OR' between them - unlike Q4, Q7 and Q10, which are labelled. They are still refd Q13a/Q13b per the pipeline convention; see the _flag on Q13a.

questions.stem: Let A and B be two events such that \(P(A) = \frac{5}{8}\), \(P(B) = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(P(A/B) = \frac{3}{4}\). Find the value of \(P(B/A)\).
Two balls are drawn at random from a bag containing 2 red balls and 3 blue balls, without replacement. Let the variable X denotes the number of red balls. Find the probability distribution of X.
questions._flag: Printed as 'Let the variable X denotes the number of red balls' - the printed subject-verb agreement is wrong ('denotes' for 'denote'). Transcribed as printed; the question is unambiguous. The identical misprint is on 65/1/1, where this is Q5.

questions.subtopic: Order and Degree of a Differential Equation
questions.stem: Find the sum of the order and the degree of the differential equation : \(\left(x + \frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 1\)
If \(\frac{d}{dx}[F(x)] = \frac{\sec^4 x}{\operatorname{cosec}^4 x}\) and \(F\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\pi}{4}\), then find \(F(x)\).
Find the values of \(\lambda\), for which the distance of point \((2, 1, \lambda)\) from plane \(3x + 5y + 4z = 11\) is \(2\sqrt{2}\) units.

If \(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + \hat{k}\) and \(\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\) are two vectors for which the vector \((\vec{a} + \vec{b})\) is perpendicular to the vector \((\vec{a} - \vec{b})\), then find all the possible values of y.

Find the co-ordinates of point where the line \(\frac{x - 3}{-1} = \frac{y + 4}{1} = \frac{z + 5}{6}\) crosses the plane passing through points \(\left(\frac{7}{2}, 0, 0\right)\), \((0, 7, 0)\) and \((0, 0, 7)\).
questions._flag: Printed as 'Find the co-ordinates of point where the line' - the article before 'point' is missing in the printed English. Transcribed as printed; the intent is unambiguous.

questions.stem: If \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), \(\vec{c}\) and \(\vec{d}\) are four non-zero vectors such that \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c} \times \vec{d}\) and \(\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = 4\vec{b} \times \vec{d}\), then show that \((\vec{a} - 2\vec{d})\) is parallel to \((2\vec{b} - \vec{c})\) where \(\vec{a} \neq 2\vec{d}\), \(\vec{c} \neq 2\vec{b}\).

The two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are represented by \(2\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}\) and \(2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\). Find the unit vectors parallel to its diagonals. Using the diagonal vectors, find the area of the parallelogram also.

A card from a pack of 52 playing cards is lost. From the remaining cards, 2 cards are drawn at random without replacement, and are found to be both aces. Find the probability that lost card being an ace.
questions._flag: Printed as 'Find the probability that lost card being an ace.' - the printed phrasing is ungrammatical (no article, participial 'being'). Transcribed as printed; the intent is unambiguous. The identical misprint is on 65/1/1, where this is Q12.

questions.stem: Using integration, find the area of the region enclosed by the curve \(y = x^2\), the \(x\)-axis and the ordinates \(x = -2\) and \(x = 1\).
questions._flag: PRINTING: unlike Q4, Q7 and Q10, this question's two branches carry NO (a)/(b) labels on the paper - the stem runs straight into a centred 'OR' and then the alternative, with the 4 marks printed only against the first. The (a)/(b) here is the pipeline's ref convention, not the paper's. The Hindi twin on idx 5 is printed the same way.

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: Using integration, find the area of the region enclosed by line \(y = \sqrt{3}x\), semi-circle \(y = \sqrt{4 - x^2}\) and \(x\)-axis in first quadrant.

questions.context:
Electrical transmission wires which are laid down in winters are stretched tightly to accommodate expansion in summers.
Two such wires lie along the following lines :
\(l_1 : \frac{x + 1}{3} = \frac{y - 3}{-2} = \frac{z + 2}{-1}\)
\(l_2 : \frac{x}{-1} = \frac{y - 7}{3} = \frac{z + 7}{-2}\)
Based on the given information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Are the lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) coplanar ? Justify your answer.
questions._figure: DECORATIVE - a captioned photograph of an electrical transmission tower (labels: Grounded metal tower, Overhead ground wires, Nearest three phase conductors, Insulators). It carries no data; both line equations are printed in the text. Page idx 6.
